# Kourovka Notebook, 17th–18th issues (lines 4883–6181): computationally tractable candidates

All 190 problems in the range were read. Problems already carrying a solution comment (17.32, 17.37, 17.42, 17.47, 17.56, 17.62, 17.75, 17.76, 17.99, 17.102, 18.1, 18.14, 18.16, 18.36, 18.38, 18.50, 18.71, 18.89) were skipped. The bulk of the remaining problems concern infinite groups, varieties, formations, orderable/topological/profinite groups or model theory and are not computer-attackable; they are omitted. Below are the candidates, ranked by score.

---

## Score 4

### 18.114 (P. Schmid) — lines 6146–6151
> 18.114. Does there exist an irreducible 5′-subgroup G of GL(V) for some finite F5-space V such that the number of conjugacy classes of the semidirect product V G is equal to |V| but G is not cyclic?
> Such a subgroup exists if 5 is replaced by p = 2, 3 but does not exist for primes p > 5 (J. Group Theory, 14 (2011), 175–199). P. Schmid

Why tractable: this is the extremal case k(GV)=|V| of the k(GV)-problem, for the single remaining prime. Everything is finite and small: V = F_5^n, G a 5′-subgroup, and k(VG) is a direct GAP computation (`NrConjugacyClasses` of `SemidirectProduct`, or via Clifford theory k(VG)=Σ_{orbit reps λ∈Irr(V)} k(G_λ)). Attack: n=1,2,3 exhaustively (irreducible soluble subgroups from the IRREDSOL package, which covers q^n ≤ 243; nonsoluble 5′-groups with faithful reps of dim ≤ 4 over F_5 are a tiny list since |G| coprime to 5 rules out A_5, L_2(4), etc.). For n=4 (|V|=625) enumerate 5′-subgroups of GL(4,5) through the Aschbacher classes: imprimitive GL(1,5)≀S_4 (order 6144, fully enumerable with `ConjugacyClassesSubgroups`), GL(2,5)≀S_2, semilinear ΓL(2,25), ΓL(1,625), tensor and extraspecial 2^{1+4}.Sp(4,2) classes — all of manageable size. Test every irreducible 5′-subgroup for k(VG)=625. An example (if it exists in small dimension) or a clean "no example for n ≤ 4" is a day's work. Score 4.

### 18.44 (T. M. Keller) — lines 5711–5715
> 18.44. Let G be a finite non-abelian group and V a finite faithful irreducible G-module. Suppose that M = |G/G′| is the largest orbit size of G on V, and among orbits of G on V there are exactly two orbits of size M. Does this imply that G is dihedral of order 8, and |V| = 9? T. M. Keller

Why tractable: a very specific claim about a finite configuration, and the hypothesis (largest orbit size = |G:G′|) makes the search space small: all orbits have size ≤ |G/G′|, so stabilizers have index ≤ |G:G′|. Attack: loop over non-abelian G in SmallGroups (say |G| ≤ 500, plus all with |G/G′| small), over small fields GF(q) (no coprimeness required), compute faithful irreducible modules with `IrreducibleModules(G, GF(q), d)` (MeatAxe), take `OrbitLengths` of G on V, and test "max = |G:G′| and exactly two orbits of size max". Any hit other than (D_8, F_3^2) answers "no"; otherwise one has strong evidence and a clean list of small cases. Score 4.

### 18.20 (V. A. Belonogov) — lines 5566–5571
> 18.20. Characters φ and ψ of a finite group G are said to be semiproportional if they are not proportional and there is a normal subset M of G such that φ|M is proportional to ψ|M and φ|G\M is proportional to ψ|G\M.
> Conjecture: If φ and ψ are semiproportional irreducible characters of a finite group, then φ(1) = ψ(1). V. A. Belonogov

Why tractable: purely a character-table property. For each pair of irreducibles of different degree, compute the ratio φ(g)/ψ(g) class by class (with the convention that classes where both vanish are free): the pair is semiproportional iff the classes can be split into two parts with constant ratio on each. Attack: run over all SmallGroups up to order 1000–2000 (`CharacterTable`), all CTblLib tables (sporadics, ATLAS groups, their extensions) and p-groups of order up to 3^7 / 2^9. Belonogov verified the conjecture for several families (S_n, A_n, sporadics) but a systematic sweep of small groups and p-groups has not been reported in the Notebook; a single counterexample settles it. Score 4.

### 18.46 (Ant. A. Klyachko) — lines 5721–5727
> 18.46. Every finite group G can be embedded in a group H in such a way that every element of G is a square of an element of H. The overgroup H can be chosen such that |H| ⩽ 2|G|². Is this estimate sharp?
> It is known that the best possible estimate cannot be better than |H| ⩽ |G|² (D. V. Baranov, Ant. A. Klyachko, Siber. Math. J., 53, no. 2 (2012), 201–206). Ant. A. Klyachko

Why tractable: for a fixed small G, the minimal |H| is a finite search: enumerate groups H of order ≤ 2|G|² (SmallGroups suffices for |G| ≤ 12, i.e. |H| ≤ 288; for |G|=16, |H| ≤ 512 is also available), find subgroups isomorphic to G (`IsomorphicSubgroups`) and check that every element of the image is a square in H (compute the set {h² : h ∈ H} once per H). Odd-order G are trivial (every element is already a square), so test G = C_2, C_2², C_4, S_3, C_6, D_8, Q_8, C_2³, C_4×C_2, D_10, D_12, A_4, Q_12, groups of order 16. If some G needs |H| = 2|G|² the bound is sharp (answer "yes"); if all small G have |H| ≤ |G|² this gives strong evidence towards the sharper bound and pinpoints where the constant 2 could come from. Score 4.

### 18.56 (G. Cutolo) — lines 5770–5774
> 18.56. Let G be a finite 2-group, of order greater than 2, such that |H/H_G| ⩽ 2 for all H ⩽ G, where H_G denotes the largest normal subgroup of G contained in H. Must G have an abelian subgroup of index 4? G. Cutolo

Why tractable: "core-2 2-groups". The condition is extremely restrictive (in particular ⟨x²⟩ ◁ G for every x, class ≤ 3, small derived subgroup by Cutolo–Khukhro–Lennox–Rinauro–Smith–Wiegold, J. Algebra 1997, where a weaker index bound for p=2 is proved). Attack: exhaustive scan of SmallGroups of order 2^n, n ≤ 8 (56 092 groups at 256) with the cheap prefilter (all ⟨x²⟩ normal, class ≤ 3), then full check of |H:H_G| ≤ 2 on `ConjugacyClassesSubgroups`, then check existence of an abelian subgroup of index ≤ 4. Order 512 (10.5 million groups) is feasible on 20 cores with the prefilter. A counterexample of order ≤ 512 settles the problem; note that a counterexample must have no abelian subgroup of index ≤ 4, which forces |G| ≥ 64. Score 4.

### 18.77 (D. S. Passman) — lines 5891–5896
> 18.77. Let G be a finite p-group and let p^e be the largest degree of an irreducible complex representation of G. If p > e, is it necessarily true that ∩ ker Θ = 1, where the intersection runs over all irreducible complex representations Θ of G of degree p^e? D. S. Passman

Why tractable: fully finite. For p=2 only e=1 is relevant (2-groups with max character degree 2: well-understood, have an abelian subgroup of index 2 or |G:Z| = 8), p=3 gives e ≤ 2 (3-groups of order ≤ 3^7 with max degree ≤ 9), p=5 gives e ≤ 4 (all 5-groups of order ≤ 5^7 qualify), p=7 all 7-groups of order ≤ 7^6. Attack: for each such group compute `CharacterDegrees`/`Irr`, take the characters of maximal degree, intersect kernels (`KernelOfCharacter`), test triviality. Either a counterexample appears (settling the problem negatively) or the small-order cases are verified; the case e=1 can likely be proved by hand from the structure of p-groups with max degree p. Score 4.

### 18.119 (P. Shumyatsky) — lines 6169–6173
> 18.119. A multilinear commutator word is any commutator of weight n in n distinct variables. Let w be a multilinear commutator word and let G be a finite group. Is it true that every Sylow p-subgroup of the verbal subgroup w(G) is generated by w-values? P. Shumyatsky

Why tractable: concrete finite check for the first nontrivial words: w = [x,y] (G′), γ_3 = [x,y,z], δ_2 = [[x,y],[z,t]] (G″), δ_3 (G‴). Known results (Acciarri–Fernández-Alcober–Shumyatsky, focal theorem for outer commutator words) give generation by *powers* of w-values, so a counterexample would be a group where the actual w-values in a Sylow subgroup P of w(G) generate a proper subgroup. Attack: over SmallGroups (orders ≤ 1000–2000 with derived length ≥ 3, plus perfect groups and small non-soluble groups), compute the set W of w-values (iteratively: commutator set of commutator set), for each prime p a Sylow P of w(G), and test ⟨P ∩ W⟩ = P. Very fast; a counterexample is quite plausible for δ_2 in a small soluble group. Score 4.

### 18.120 (E. Jabara) — lines 6174–6178
> 18.120. Let P = AB be a finite p-group factorized by an abelian subgroup A and a class-two subgroup B. Suppose, if necessary, A ∩ B = 1. Then is it true that ⟨A, [B, B]⟩ = AB_0, where B_0 is an abelian subgroup of B? E. Jabara

Why tractable: a statement about factorizations of small p-groups. Attack: for each P of order 2^n (n ≤ 8), 3^n (n ≤ 6), 5^5: enumerate subgroup classes, take abelian A and class-2 B with |A||B|/|A∩B| = |P| and AB = P (test on conjugates), form C = ⟨A, B′⟩ and test whether C = A·B_0 for some abelian B_0 ≤ B (B_0 ranges over abelian subgroups of B with |A||B_0|/|A∩B_0| = |C| and B_0 ≤ C). Run first with A∩B = 1. A counterexample among 2-groups of order ≤ 256 or 3-groups of order ≤ 729 would settle it; no counterexample gives a verified range. Score 4.

### 17.128 (E. Jabara) — lines 5477–5480
> 17.128. Let T be a finite p-group admitting an elementary abelian group of automorphisms A of order p² such that in the semidirect product P = T A every element of P \ T has order p. Does it follow that T is of exponent p? E. Jabara

Why tractable: p = 2 is a two-line argument (a, b, ab all invert T ⇒ T has exponent 2), and abelian T is also elementary: the p+1 subgroups of order p of A partition A\{1}, so Σ_{c} N_c = p·1 + N_A acts as 0 on T while each N_c acts as 0, forcing pT = 0. So the problem is really about non-abelian T and odd p, where a finite search is natural. Attack: for each P in SmallGroups of order 3^n (n ≤ 7; n = 8 with filters on 20 cores) and 5^n (n ≤ 6): find normal T of index p² with P/T elementary abelian and complemented (A ≅ C_p²), check that all elements of P\T have order p (element orders from `ConjugacyClasses`), and record exponent of T. A non-abelian T of exponent p² would be a counterexample; the computations also suggest the shape of a proof (via the p+1 subgroups of A). Score 4.

### 17.1 (I. M. Isaacs / A. Abdollahi) — lines 4885–4887

Remaining candidates (compact), continuing from 17.45(c):

**17.45 c) (Vdovin–Revin), lines 5074–5081 — score 3.** Is a Hall subgroup with a Sylow tower always strongly pronormal in a finite group? Trivially true in soluble groups (Hall's theorem), so counterexamples must be non-soluble. Attack: scan small non-soluble groups (orders ≤ 10^4–10^5, perfect-group library, almost simple groups) for Hall π-subgroups H with a Sylow tower; for each L ≤ H (class reps) and g, test whether L^g is conjugate into H inside ⟨H, L^g⟩ (`IsConjugate` in the subgroup). A counterexample would be decisive.

**18.84 (Revin), lines 5925–5931 — score 3.** BS_π-groups (Baer–Suzuki property for a set π of primes): is every normal subgroup of a BS_π-group again BS_π? Known "yes" if 2 ∉ π. Attack: for π ∋ 2 (e.g. {2,3}, {2,5}, {2,3,5}), test the BS_π property class-by-class on small non-soluble groups (A_5×H, wreath/subdirect constructions, groups of order ≤ 10^5) and on their normal subgroups; look for G BS_π with N ◁ G not BS_π.

**18.64 (Harada's conjecture, via Mazurov), lines 5815–5821 — score 3.** For a p-block B, if a non-empty J ⊆ Irr(B) satisfies Σ_{χ∈J} χ(1)χ(g) = 0 for all p-singular g, then J = Irr(B). Attack: for all CTblLib tables (sporadics, ATLAS groups) and SmallGroups, compute blocks (`PrimeBlocks`), set up the linear system on the p-singular classes, and search {0,1}-solutions in its rational kernel (enumeration when the kernel is small, ILP otherwise). A counterexample settles it; verification for all library tables is a solid special case.

**17.80 (Macedońska), lines 5227–5231 — score 3.** Is M_n = ⟨x,y | x = [x,_n y], y = [y,_n x]⟩ infinite for every n > 2? M_n is perfect. Attack for n = 3, 4, 5: `LowIndexSubgroupsFpGroup` up to index ~20–30 and `AbelianInvariants` of the subgroups (a finite-index subgroup with infinite abelianisation proves infiniteness); alternatively `GQuotients` onto small simple groups, KBMAG/coset enumeration to rule out small finite order.

**17.5 (Abdollahi), lines 4896–4898 — score 3.** Is the class of a nilpotent group generated by d left 3-Engel elements bounded in terms of d (known ≤ 4 for d = 2)? Attack: use the NQ package with identical generators to compute the largest nilpotent quotient of ⟨x_1,…,x_d⟩ subject to the laws [g, x_i, x_i, x_i] = 1 (g universally quantified) for d = 3 and 4; if the lower central series stabilises one gets the exact class bound for that d, which is a new concrete result.

**18.58 (Lytkina), lines 5775–5781 — score 3.** A group generated by n involutions in which (uv)^4 = 1 for all involutions u, v: finite? a 2-group? Known for n ≤ 3; n = 4 is the first open case, and the class of such quotients of the Coxeter group C = ⟨a,b,c,d | a², …, (ab)^4, …, (cd)^4⟩ is closed under subdirect products, so a universal group U exists. Attack: iterate 2-quotient (`PQuotient`/`EpimorphismPGroup`) of C, add relators (uv)^4 for all involution pairs of the current finite quotient, repeat until stable; then verify the property in the resulting finite 2-group (which would then equal U and settle n = 4).

J. 2022) — check their paper first, as it may already cover some denominators in this interval.

**17.112 (Skiba–Tyutyanov), lines 5395–5407 — score 3.** Which finite non-abelian simple groups have a nontrivial (hereditarily) G-permutable subgroup? Sporadics done (only J_1 for (a)). Attack: for A_n (n ≤ 9), PSL(2,q) (q ≤ 32), L_3(3), U_3(3), M_11, … compute all subgroup classes and test for A whether every subgroup class B has a conjugate with AB^x = B^x A; the outcome for small groups of Lie type suggests/decides the pattern for PSL(2,q) and rank-1 groups.
